title: Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData & Vector Stores
description: Master the unified Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData abstractions for vector databases in .NET.

data.text: Just as Microsoft.Extensions.AI provides unified abstractions for chat and embedding models, Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData provides a standardized, provider-agnostic abstraction layer for vector databases in .NET. Instead of binding your data access layer directly to Qdrant, Azure AI Search, Milvus, Redis, or PostgreSQL pgvector SDKs, you code against IVectorStore and IVectorStoreRecordCollection<TKey, TRecord>.

data.title: Why Unified Abstractions Matter
data.text: In enterprise applications, vector store requirements often evolve. A team might start prototyping with an in-memory or embedded vector store, deploy to Qdrant or Azure AI Search in staging, and leverage pgvector in production. Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData decouples domain models and ingestion logic from the underlying storage engine.
Records in Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData use declarative attributes to define the primary key, metadata payload fields, and dense vector embeddings with dimensions and distance metrics.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData standardizes vector database interactions in .NET
Use IVectorStore and IVectorStoreRecordCollection<TKey, TRecord> for provider portability
VectorSearchFilter provides strongly-typed metadata filtering for tenant isolation and security ACLs
Switch between Azure AI Search, Qdrant, Redis, or pgvector by swapping DI registration without changing application code
data.takeaway: Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData eliminates vendor lock-in for vector databases, allowing .NET teams to write portable, testable RAG ingestion and retrieval layers.
